title: European Stroke Organisation (ESO) - European Society for Minimally Invasive Neurological Therapy (ESMINT) Guidelines on Mechanical Thrombectomy in Acute Ischaemic Stroke, Endorsed by Stroke Alliance for Europe (SAFE)

recommendations.section: PICO 1: MT plus BMM versus BMM alone within 6 hours of symptom onset
recommendations.text: In adults with anterior circulation LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke presenting within 6 hours after symptom onset, we recommend MT plus BMM, including IVT whenever indicated, over BMM alone to improve functional outcome.

recommendations.section: PICO 1: MT plus BMM versus BMM alone within 6 hours of symptom onset - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: There is a consensus among the guideline group (11/11 votes) that patients with M2 occlusion fulfilled the inclusion criteria in most randomized trials and therefore mechanical thrombectomy is reasonable in this situation.
recommendations.currentEvidenceNote: Historical 2019 consensus. The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline distinguishes selected dominant proximal M2 occlusion from nondominant/codominant proximal M2 and more distal occlusions; this older unrestricted M2 statement should not be used as a universal EVT indication.

recommendations.section: PICO 1: MT plus BMM versus BMM alone within 6 hours of symptom onset - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: There is a consensus among the panel (11/11 votes) that in analogy to anterior circulation LVO and with regard to the grim natural course of basilar artery occlusions, the therapeutic approach with IVT plus MT should strongly be considered.

recommendations.section: PICO 2: MT plus BMM versus BMM alone 6 to 24 hours from time last known well
recommendations.text: In adults with anterior circulation LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke presenting between 6 and 24 hours from time last known well and fulfilling the selection criteria of DEFUSE-3 or DAWN, we recommend MT plus BMM over BMM alone to improve functional outcome.

recommendations.section: PICO 2: MT plus BMM versus BMM alone 6 to 24 hours from time last known well - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: Patients should be treated with MT plus BMM up to approximately 7 hours 18 min after stroke onset, without the need of perfusion imaging-based selection.

recommendations.section: PICO 2: MT plus BMM versus BMM alone 6 to 24 hours from time last known well - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: 10/11 experts agree that patients can be treated in the 6-12 hour time window if they fulfil the ESCAPE criteria, notably ASPECTS >= 6 and moderate-to-good collateral circulation. However, such patients should preferably be treated in the context of clinical studies. Also, concurrent software applications utilizing similar perfusion algorithms and rendering equivalent volumetry results as those used in the DAWN and DEFUSE-3 trials may be options, as well as simple volumetry on a high quality DWI scan for core volume when applying DAWN criteria.

recommendations.section: PICO 3: IVT plus MT versus MT alone
recommendations.text: In LVO-related ischaemic stroke patients eligible for both treatments, we recommend IVT plus MT over MT alone. Both treatments should be performed as early as possible after hospital arrival. MT should not prevent the initiation of IVT, and IVT should not delay MT.

recommendations.section: PICO 3: IVT plus MT versus MT alone
recommendations.text: In LVO-related ischaemic stroke patients not eligible for IVT, we recommend MT as standalone treatment.

recommendations.section: PICO 3: IVT plus MT versus MT alone - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: In LVO-related ischaemic stroke patients eligible for IVT before MT, 7/11 experts suggest the use of tenecteplase (0.25 mg/kg) over alteplase (0.9 mg/kg) if the decision on IVT is made after vessel occlusion status is known.

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Use of a prehospital scale in suspected acute stroke
recommendations.text: In patients with suspected stroke, we cannot make a recommendation on the use of a prehospital scale for improving identification of patients eligible for MT. We suggest enrolling patients in a dedicated randomized controlled trial, whenever possible. (Quality of evidence: Very low; the guideline assigned no strength of recommendation.)

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Use of a prehospital scale in suspected acute stroke - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: 11/11 experts concluded that there is currently not enough evidence to use a clinical scale in routine care to help triage potential thrombectomy candidates in the prehospital field.

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Use of a prehospital scale in suspected acute stroke - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: All patients suspected of having an acute stroke, irrespective of the time of onset, should undergo emergency imaging of the brain, including vascular imaging.

recommendations.section: PICO 5: Mothership versus drip-and-ship model
recommendations.text: We cannot make recommendations on whether for adults identified as potential candidates for MT in the prehospital field, the mothership or the drip-and-ship model should be applied to improve functional outcome. (Quality of evidence: Very low; the guideline assigned no strength of recommendation.)

recommendations.section: PICO 5: Mothership versus drip-and-ship model - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: As there is lack of strong evidence for superiority of one organizational model, the choice of model should depend on local and regional service organization and patient characteristics (vote: 11/11 experts agree).

recommendations.section: PICO 5: Mothership versus drip-and-ship model - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: The mothership model might be favored in metropolitan areas, with transportation time to a comprehensive stroke center of less than 30-45 minutes, and the use of the drip-and-ship model when transportation times are longer (vote: 11/11 experts agree).

recommendations.section: PICO 5: Mothership versus drip-and-ship model - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: As there is limited experience with the other two models (drip-and-drive and mobile stroke unit) no expert opinion can be provided when to use these models (vote: 11/11 experts agree).

recommendations.section: PICO 6: MT in patients aged 80 years or more
recommendations.text: We recommend that patients aged 80 years or more with LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke within 6 hours of symptom onset should be treated with MT plus BMM, including IVT whenever indicated. Application of an upper age limit for MT is not justified.

recommendations.section: PICO 6: MT in patients aged 80 years or more
recommendations.text: We suggest that patients aged 80 years or more with LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke between 6 and 24 hours from time last known well should be treated with MT plus BMM if they meet the eligibility criteria of the DEFUSE-3 or DAWN trials. (Strength of recommendation: Weak.)

recommendations.section: PICO 7: Selection of MT candidates by NIHSS score threshold
recommendations.text: We do not recommend an upper NIHSS score limit for decision-making on MT. We recommend that patients with high stroke severity and LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke be treated with MT plus BMM, including IVT whenever indicated. These recommendations also apply for patients in the 6-24 h time window, provided that they meet the inclusion criteria for the DAWN or DEFUSE-3 studies.

recommendations.section: PICO 7: Selection of MT candidates by NIHSS score threshold
recommendations.text: We recommend that patients with low stroke severity (NIHSS 0-5) and LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke within 24 hours from time last known well be included in randomized controlled trials comparing MT plus BMM versus BMM alone. (Quality of evidence: Very low; the guideline assigned no strength of recommendation.)

recommendations.section: PICO 7: Selection of MT candidates by NIHSS score threshold - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: In patients with a low NIHSS score (0-5) who are not eligible for a dedicated randomized controlled trial, we suggest that treatment with mechanical thrombectomy in addition to intravenous thrombolysis (or alone in case of contraindication to intravenous thrombolysis) may be reasonable in patients with deficits that appear disabling (e.g. significant motor deficit or aphasia or hemianopia) at presentation (vote: 9/11 experts).

recommendations.section: PICO 7: Selection of MT candidates by NIHSS score threshold - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: In patients with a low NIHSS score (0-5) who are not eligible for a dedicated randomized controlled trial, mechanical thrombectomy may be reasonable in the case of clinical worsening despite intravenous thrombolysis (vote: 9/11 experts).

recommendations.section: PICO 7: Selection of MT candidates by NIHSS score threshold - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: We did not reach a majority vote to suggest mechanical thrombectomy in patients with deficits that appear non-disabling (e.g. mild hypoesthesia) at presentation (vote: 5/11 experts).

recommendations.section: PICO 8: Selection of MT candidates by ASPECTS or infarct core volume threshold
recommendations.text: In the 0-6 hour time window, we recommend MT plus BMM (including IVT whenever indicated) over BMM alone in LVO-related anterior circulation stroke patients without evidence of extensive infarct core (e.g. ASPECTS >= 6 on non-contrast CT scan or infarct core volume <= 70 ml).

recommendations.section: PICO 8: Selection of MT candidates by ASPECTS or infarct core volume threshold
recommendations.text: In the 6-24 hour time window, we recommend MT plus BMM (including IVT whenever indicated) over BMM alone in LVO-related anterior circulation stroke patients fulfilling the selection criteria of DEFUSE-3 or DAWN, including estimated volume of infarct core.

recommendations.section: PICO 8: Selection of MT candidates by ASPECTS or infarct core volume threshold
recommendations.text: We recommend that anterior circulation stroke patients with extensive infarct core (e.g. ASPECTS < 6 on non-contrast CT scan or core volume > 70 ml or > 100 ml) be included in RCTs comparing mechanical thrombectomy plus best medical management versus best medical management alone. (Quality of evidence: Very low; the guideline assigned no strength of recommendation.) [Current-evidence note: outdated — 2023 RCTs in anterior-circulation LVO with large infarct core (e.g., SELECT2: ASPECTS 3-5 or core ≥50 ml within 24 h; TENSION: ASPECTS 3-5 within 12 h) showed better functional outcomes with thrombectomy than medical care alone.]

recommendations.section: PICO 8: Selection of MT candidates by ASPECTS or infarct core volume threshold - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: If inclusion of the patient in a dedicated randomized controlled trial is not possible, we suggest that treatment with MT may be reasonable on an individual basis in selected cases with ASPECTS < 6 or core volume > 70 ml (11/11 experts agree). Patient selection criteria might include age, severity and type of neurological impairment, time since symptom onset, location of the ischaemic lesion on plain CT scanner or MRI, and results of advanced imaging, notably perfusion-core mismatch.

recommendations.section: PICO 9: Selection of MT candidates based on advanced perfusion, core, or collateral imaging
recommendations.text: In adult patients with anterior circulation LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke presenting from 0-6 hours from time last known well, advanced imaging is not necessary for patient selection. (Strength of recommendation: Weak against.)

recommendations.section: PICO 9: Selection of MT candidates based on advanced perfusion, core, or collateral imaging
recommendations.text: In adult patients with anterior circulation LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke presenting beyond 6 hours from time last known well, advanced imaging selection is necessary.
recommendations.currentEvidenceNote: Historical 2019 imaging requirement. The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline permits appropriately selected late-window EVT pathways using CT/CTA criteria; perfusion imaging is not a universal prerequisite for every patient beyond 6 hours.

recommendations.section: PICO 10: MT performed in a comprehensive stroke center
recommendations.text: In adult patients with LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke, we recommend treatment in a comprehensive stroke center.

recommendations.section: PICO 11: TICI Grade 3 versus TICI Grade 2b reperfusion
recommendations.text: For adults with LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke, we recommend that interventionalists should attempt a TICI Grade 3 reperfusion, if achievable with reasonable safety.

recommendations.section: PICO 12: Direct aspiration versus stent retriever
recommendations.text: There is currently no evidence that contact aspiration alone improves functional outcome compared with BMM in patients undergoing MT. There is currently no evidence that contact aspiration alone increases the rate of reperfusion over thrombectomy using a stent retriever. Therefore, we suggest the use of a stent retriever over contact aspiration alone for MT in patients with acute ischaemic stroke. (Strength of recommendation: Weak for.)

recommendations.section: PICO 12: Direct aspiration versus stent retriever - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: 9/11 experts believe that ADAPT may be used as standard first-line treatment, followed by stent retriever thrombectomy as rescue therapy if needed.

recommendations.section: PICO 12: Direct aspiration versus stent retriever - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: We did not reach a majority vote that distal aspiration should be used only in combination with a stent-retriever (3/11 experts).

recommendations.section: PICO 12: Direct aspiration versus stent retriever - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: 8/11 experts believe that any MT procedure should be performed preferably in conjunction with a proximal balloon guide catheter.

recommendations.section: PICO 13: Conscious sedation versus general anaesthesia during MT
recommendations.text: We cannot provide recommendations to use general anesthesia or conscious sedation in patients undergoing MT, due to a low quality of evidence and conflicting results between 3 small single-center randomized clinical trials and the best available observational evidence. Therefore, we recommend the enrollment of patients in multicenter randomized controlled trials addressing this question. (Quality of evidence: Very low; the guideline assigned no strength of recommendation.)

recommendations.section: PICO 13: Conscious sedation versus general anaesthesia during MT - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: If inclusion of the patient in a randomized controlled trial is not possible, 11/11 experts suggest that local anesthesia or conscious sedation may be favored over general anesthesia, if the patient is able to undergo MT without general anesthesia. General anesthesia does not need to be avoided if indicated. The decision for or against general anesthesia should be made rapidly and delays to induction of general anesthesia should be minimized. A specialized neuro-anesthesiological or neurocritical care team should perform the general anesthesia procedure, whenever possible. Excessive blood pressure drops should be avoided. Adequate monitoring of vital parameters of patients under conscious sedation or local anesthesia is also advised.

recommendations.section: PICO 14: Blood pressure targets during and after MT
recommendations.text: We suggest to keep blood pressure below 180/105 mmHg during and 24 hours after MT. No specific blood pressure-lowering drug can be recommended. (Strength of recommendation: Weak for.)

recommendations.section: PICO 14: Blood pressure targets during and after MT
recommendations.text: During MT, systolic blood pressure drops should be avoided. (Strength of recommendation: Strong against.)

recommendations.section: PICO 14: Blood pressure targets during and after MT - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: 11/11 experts think that the degree of reperfusion should be taken into account in the choice of a blood pressure target after MT, with a lower blood pressure target in case of complete reperfusion. [Current-evidence note: superseded — later RCTs (ENCHANTED2/MT, OPTIMAL-BP) found worse outcomes with intensive post-thrombectomy BP lowering, and the 2025 ESO BP update recommends against actively lowering systolic BP to <140 mmHg in the first 24 h after successful thrombectomy (strong recommendation, high certainty).]

recommendations.section: PICO 15: Cervical stenting in addition to MT for high-grade extracranial carotid stenosis
recommendations.text: No recommendation can be provided regarding which treatment modality should be favored in patients with LVO-related acute ischaemic stroke and associated extracranial carotid artery stenosis or occlusion. We recommend the inclusion of such patients in dedicated randomized controlled trials. (Quality of evidence: Very low; the guideline assigned no strength of recommendation.)

recommendations.section: PICO 15: Cervical stenting in addition to MT for high-grade extracranial carotid stenosis - Expert opinion
recommendations.text: 9/11 experts suggest that if inclusion in a dedicated randomized controlled trial is not possible, patients with high-grade stenosis or occlusion may be treated with intra-procedural stenting if unavoidably needed.

sourceReview.scope: Source wording, grading and publication updates were compared at the available source depth. This is not certification of comprehensive current clinical guidance.
sourceReview.sourceAccess: Primary recommendation text retrieved and compared; exact edition, source locators and unresolved correction/current-context limits in unit ledger.
sourceReview.currencyNote: Identified extraction defects have been repaired. Selected later evidence is labeled separately in dated current-evidence notes; absence of an update note does not establish comprehensive clinical currency.
sourceReview.sourceEditionNote: Attributions retain the original publication identity. The source-access description and individual correction notices define the edition limits.
